notes: The page is a typescript headed Compléments sur transformation de Coxeter d’un système de racines, with a circled handwritten irreducibility qualifier and an English reference to The principal 3-dimensional subgroup ... th. 9.2.

Statement a) asserts bounds on eigenvalue orders using m_i+1 and h, an order-h criterion for Coxeter transformations, and regularity of the corresponding nonzero eigenvectors. Its dimension-one qualification is a left marginal insertion.

The first corollary identifies the cyclic group μ with its centralizer and states that the normalizer quotient maps isomorphically to Aut(μ). The right-hand question asks which extension is obtained; the left note proposes exchanging with corollary 3.

The proof uses the one-dimensional primitive eigenspace D, a finite cyclic image in Aut(D), a retraction onto μ, and regularity to argue that the kernel is trivial. It then attributes conjugacy of coprime powers to Kostant. These are statements read, not independently established theorems.

The second corollary states that an eigenvector of a Coxeter element is regular exactly when its eigenvalue is a primitive h-th root. The following paragraph gives the sufficiency reference and the necessity argument.

The bottom begins another corollary about a regular line in V with a circled-x/tensor-like composite and underlined C. It ends physically with élé-. The reading keeps the C-style page-continuation form élé% rather than supplying the missing rest of the word.

Explicit questions or proof obligations: “Quelle extension ... obtient-on ?”; “il faut prouver que son noyau est réduit à 1” is followed by the kernel argument; “Reste à prouver ... ce qui résulte également de Kostant” is an attribution, not an openly unfinished proof on this page.

No manuscript date, authorial page number or stated total page count was observed. Archive sheet number 1 is in the lower-left corner and appears only as a comment. Packet metadata identifies our scan 2 with H page 1.

The source’s c^h in the first conjugacy formula, droite régulières and conjugué de c are retained literally. The algebraic difficulty with c^h prompted comparison of that exponent with the later c^n; no correction was made.

The top z-shaped portions of the four centralizer glyphs are typed, with lower handwritten additions. The reading uses the existing handwritten wrapper for the composite and explicitly records the mixed construction here; it does not claim the entire visible glyph was penned.
Whole image dimensions: 1672 by 2144 pixels. Each half: 1672 by 1152. Half a corresponds to whole y=0–1152; half b to y=992–2144. Every reported bbox uses whole-image coordinates.

Visible canceled words were retained, including une droite, induit, the top Considérons and the lower Soit D une. For the short heavy mechanical overprints est, en, un and Bn/On, no secure earlier complete word or correction order was inferred.

math_checks.performed: Using the statement’s order-h premise, c^h=1. The displayed equality would then imply c=1 by conjugation, inconsistent with order h>1. This checks only that local consequence.
math_checks.result: The source exponent h was retained because its tall ascender is visible. The later c^n is a distinct, clearly shorter exponent. No theorem about root systems was verified.

math_checks.check: Targeted divisibility step at the end of the necessity proof
math_checks.performed: Assuming c has order h and h′ is a positive eigenvalue order, c^{h′}=1 implies h divides h′. Together with 1≤h′≤h this forces h′=h.
math_checks.result: The final arithmetic implication is consistent under those premises. The regularity-to-centralizer step and the earlier eigenvalue bound were not independently proved.

workflow_feedback: Completed one whole-page view, one view of each half, then one view of each of 18 targeted crops. No crop or half was reloaded, and no other page, witness packet, reader output, root decision, OCR or external source was consulted. The rotated left note and tight bottom crop were especially useful. Overprint chronology remains a genuine limit; the report distinguishes visible traces from reconstructed originals.
